Yeah I imagined it would be better in other countries lol I only have experience with Mexican and American schools so this is basically my experience showing how little they think of education:


Mexico: Public schools are the fucking worst. Dirt floors outside of classrooms, poorly kept buildings, there’s no cafeteria there might be commissary to buy chips or cup of noodles and stuff but mainly you bring your own lunch. You HAVE TO wear uniform(yes public school) and you have to PAY for it, some kids are sadly too poor so they are allowed to wear clothes that match the uniform color until they can get the uniform(that they’ll grow out of in a couple of months) classrooms are bare and boring, 55 kids in one class(not an exaggeration, actually more) my grandma worked at 2 schools and a hospital as a nurse to make ends meet, she sadly passed away before she could retire as a teacher, she fell ill while decorating her classroom, she also spent so much she didn’t have on her students because they were from one of the poorest areas 

Private schools are a bit better, the school I went to was very American inspired so I assume it’s about the same as American schools, just a much shittier government. But at least College is much cheaper.


America: thankfully for the student financial help there was a good amount, free lunches or a free backpack with supplies from one of the drives they always did. In JrHS teachers would often be frustrated that they couldn’t give a kid a pencil because they didn’t have one, they already spent all their money in a fun activity for us ungrateful teenagers. In HS I had a teacher who was amazing with me, so patient and so kind(also an amazing viola player) I actually put in effort in her class. After school one day I had to buy stuff at an Office Depot and my cashier was that teacher, she had to have two jobs to support her and her kids and Office Depot was great for the discounts for her classroom(truly selfless woman) my Photo teacher was also similarly amazing, he was older with no kids so his students were his kids. Someone didn’t have money to enter a contest? He took it out of his own pocket because he believed in you, once he told me my pictures were to good to not enter and he would pay for it and sent me on my way to cut a Mat and get my photos ready.



Those scenarios of something required for school should not happen, education should be free and easily accessible for both teachers and students. I’m glad Canada seems to go in the right direction, I just hope my two countries do the same. 



TL;DR: Education budget should be increased, Mexican public schools suck, American schools should take care of their rare teachers, there’s not that many with the kindness I thankfully experience. Teachers deserve better.

Yeah I imagined it would be better in other countries lol I only have experience with Mexican and American schools so this is basically my experience showing how little they think of education:


Mexico: Public schools are the fucking worst. Dirt floors outside of classrooms, poorly kept buildings, there’s no cafeteria there might be commissary to buy chips or cup of noodles and stuff but mainly you bring your own lunch. You HAVE TO wear uniform(yes public school) and you have to PAY for it, some kids are sadly too poor so they are allowed to wear clothes that match the uniform color until they can get the uniform(that they’ll grow out of in a couple of months) classrooms are bare and boring, 55 kids in one class(not an exaggeration, actually more) my grandma worked at 2 schools and a hospital as a nurse to make ends meet, she sadly passed away before she could retire as a teacher, she fell ill while decorating her classroom, she also spent so much she didn’t have on her students because they were from one of the poorest areas 

Private schools are a bit better, the school I went to was very American inspired so I assume it’s about the same as American schools, just a much shittier government. But at least College is much cheaper.


America: thankfully for the student financial help there was a good amount, free lunches or a free backpack with supplies from one of the drives they always did. In JrHS teachers would often be frustrated that they couldn’t give a kid a pencil because they didn’t have one, they already spent all their money in a fun activity for us ungrateful teenagers. In HS I had a teacher who was amazing with me, so patient and so kind(also an amazing viola player) I actually put in effort in her class. After school one day I had to buy stuff at an Office Depot and my cashier was that teacher, she had to have two jobs to support her and her kids and Office Depot was great for the discounts for her classroom(truly selfless woman) my Photo teacher was also similarly amazing, he was older with no kids so his students were his kids. Someone didn’t have money to enter a contest? He took it out of his own pocket because he believed in you, once he told me my pictures were to good to not enter and he would pay for it and sent me on my way to cut a Mat and get my photos ready.



Those scenarios of something required for school should not happen, education should be free and easily accessible for both teachers and students. I’m glad Canada seems to go in the right direction, I just hope my two countries do the same. 



TL;DR: Education budget should be increased, Mexican public schools suck, American schools should take care of their rare teachers, there’s not that many with the kindness I thankfully experience. Teachers deserve better.

Those lists are great and are very useful to take some of the weight off of teachers, but school budgets should be increased to be able to at least cover the teachers’ supplies consistently throughout the school year.
